issues.description: Stats counter allocated then immediately discarded; spec of override path is incoherent
issues.detail: In the non-detailed override branch, the code calls `NewRateLimit(..., this.statsManager.NewStats(rateLimit.FullKey), ...)` only to overwrite `rateLimit.Stats` on the very next line with `this.statsManager.NewStats(enhancedKey)`. The first NewStats call registers a counter under the old key with no caller, leaking a stats handle on every GetLimit invocation for value_to_metric descriptors. The author cannot state a precondition under which the first allocation is needed; it is dead work whose only effect is to pollute the stats registry. UNREASONED.

issues.description: Override condition `enhancedKey != rateLimit.FullKey` is wrong as a guard for the value_to_metric feature
issues.detail: The intended postcondition is: when any ancestor descriptor has `value_to_metric: true` and matched a runtime value, stats use the enhanced key; otherwise stats are unchanged. The implemented condition instead asks whether the constructed string differs from `rateLimit.FullKey`. These are not the same predicate: with no flags set anywhere, both keys can coincide accidentally, but the override branch still fires whenever the strings happen to differ for unrelated reasons (e.g., a future change to how `FullKey` is built upstream). The flag `valueToMetric` is never consulted at the decision site. TESTED-NOT-PROVED: the unit tests cover happy paths, but the guarding invariant is not the one the author claims.

issues.description: `rateLimit` is mutated in place across requests, but `GetLimit` is called concurrently
issues.detail: `rateLimit` is the shared `*RateLimit` stored in the descriptor tree at config-load time. The new code writes `rateLimit.Stats = ...` and `rateLimit.FullKey = ...` on every call, and in the override branch even reassigns the local pointer via `NewRateLimit(...)` after mutating the shared value. The rate limit service serves many concurrent requests against the same config; two requests for the same leaf descriptor with different runtime values will race on `Stats`/`FullKey` and one will observe the other's key. The existing `detailed_metric` branch already had the same shape — the author has inherited a bug rather than reasoning about it — but this PR amplifies it by making the mutation fire on the common path, not just for detailed metrics. No invariant is stated for shared mutability; none holds. SMUGGLED-GOTO via shared mutable state.

issues.description: Unbounded stats cardinality with no guard — exactly the failure mode the `detailed_metric` warning was added for
issues.detail: `statsManager.NewStats(enhancedKey)` is invoked on every request, with `enhancedKey` derived from arbitrary runtime entry values (e.g., `route_<anything>`). Each unique runtime value allocates a fresh stats handle that is, by construction, retained by the stats store. `detailed_metric` carries an explicit NB warning in the README about cardinality; `value_to_metric` carries the same risk because runtime values are equally unbounded, yet the README sells it as a *lower*-cardinality alternative. The reasoning is backwards: cardinality is a property of the value space, not of which descriptors opt in. REFUSED until either (a) the docs honestly state the risk and (b) there is a bound or memoization on `NewStats` per key.

issues.description: Control flow in the per-entry block is unstructured; three branches collapse to one
issues.detail: The new per-entry block has three arms (`matchedViaWildcard`, `matchedUsingValue`, default-key) that each contain the same conditional: `if nextDescriptor.valueToMetric { key+"_"+value (if value!="") } else { key }`. Two of the three arms are textually identical. The structured form is: compute `includeValue := nextDescriptor.valueToMetric || matchedUsingValue`, then a single write. As written, the reader must simulate three near-duplicate branches to convince themselves the postcondition holds. This is SMUGGLED-GOTO: control flow shaped by copy-paste rather than by the property it intends to enforce.

issues.description: `matchedUsingValue` is set before fallback and then flipped — invariant is fragile
issues.detail: `matchedUsingValue := nextDescriptor != nil` is computed *after* the wildcard branch but *before* the default-key fallback, and then reset to `false` inside the fallback `if`. This is a flag-as-goto: the meaning of `matchedUsingValue` depends on the order of two later statements. A small refactor in the fallback would silently break the metric key. State the loop invariant — "after this block, matchedUsingValue is true iff descriptor was matched by explicit key+value" — and the structure that maintains it directly is a small switch over (wildcard, exact, default), not a mutable flag.

issues.description: `valueToMetricFullKey` keeps building after `break` exit, then is discarded
issues.detail: The for loop has multiple `break` paths (limit found, descriptor not found). The `valueToMetricFullKey` is appended to before those breaks but never trimmed afterward; in some control paths it contains a trailing partial segment that is never read because the leaf is reached on a prior iteration. This is harmless today because the string is only consumed at the end, but the invariant "valueToMetricFullKey corresponds to the matched prefix at the current iteration" is not actually maintained — it just happens to agree at the loop-exit iteration. State and maintain the invariant, or stop pretending to maintain it.

issues.description: `nextDescriptor == nil` branch still appends `entry.Key` to the enhanced builder, producing a key for a path that has no rate limit
issues.detail: When no descriptor matches, the code appends `entry.Key` to `valueToMetricFullKey` and comments "still append something deterministic." Determinism is not the property you want here; correctness is. If `nextDescriptor` is nil, the loop either breaks out shortly or `rateLimit` stays nil and the whole enhanced key is thrown away — so the append is dead. Dead code in a hot path is a smell that the author did not reason about which states are reachable. UNREASONED.

issues.description: `FullKey` semantics silently changed for the detailed_metric path
issues.detail: Previously the detailed-metric branch only updated `rateLimit.Stats`. This PR also writes `rateLimit.FullKey = detailedKey`. That is a behavior change for any existing caller that reads `FullKey` (logs, debug output) and was relying on the prior value. The PR description does not call this out; the test `TestValueToMetric_FullKeyMatchesStatsKey` *encodes* the new invariant but does not justify why the old invariant was wrong. State the invariant `FullKey == Stats.Key` as a deliberate design decision in the type, or revert.

issues.description: README claim that `value_to_metric` provides lower cardinality than `detailed_metric` is unsupported
issues.detail: The PR text and README frame `value_to_metric` as a way to get visibility "without...high cardinality" of `detailed_metric`. But cardinality is per descriptor times the size of the value space at that level; enabling `value_to_metric` at the top descriptors (as in Example 10) can yield identical or higher cardinality than `detailed_metric` at a leaf. The marketing does not match the math.

issues.description: Test names assert behavior; none assert the invariant
issues.detail: Every new test is a worked example of input/output strings. None states the property: `enhanced_key(d) = join(domain, segments(d))` where `segment(entry, desc) = key + ("_"+value if includeValue(entry, desc) else "")`. Property-based reasoning would have caught the wildcard/empty-value/default-key interactions in one stroke. Testing shows the presence of bugs, not their absence.

review.summary: The feature is plausibly useful, but the patch was written, not reasoned. Three problems stand out and would justify refusal at this stage: (1) the override branch in `GetLimit` calls `NewStats` twice and discards the first, registering an unused counter on every request; (2) the override decision is guarded by `enhancedKey != FullKey`, which is not the predicate the feature actually wants and only happens to agree with it on the test cases provided; (3) the shared `*RateLimit` value is mutated in place under what is a concurrent request path, racing on `Stats` and `FullKey`. The per-entry control flow is also a copy-pasted three-way branch that collapses to a single `includeValue := nextDescriptor.valueToMetric || matchedUsingValue` write — the current shape is a smuggled goto via flags. The cardinality story in the README is, on the math, the opposite of what is claimed. REFUSED in current form; would accept once the override is gated on a real predicate, the shared state is not mutated, and the per-entry block is restructured to expose its invariant.
